issue_context.title: Introduce `MatchLabelKeys` (the same one as Pod Topology Spread) to `PodAffinityTerm`
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Introduce `MatchLabelKeys` to [PodAffinityTerm](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#PodAffinityTerm) (like [we do to Pod Topology Spread](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-scheduling/3243-respect-pod-topology-spread-after-rolling-upgrades)).

### Why is this needed?

Currently, the scheduler doesn’t treat `Terminating` Pods as removed Pods.
See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/105661. Pod Topology Spreading gets imbalanced after Deployment/Replicaset upgrades because of that. So, we introduced `MatchLabelKeys` to Pod Topology Spread (https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3243).

In Pod Affinity and Pod Anti Affinity, it gives a negative impact on the scheduling result to take old Pods into account during scheduling (“Old Pods” = Pods from a old deployment); Old pods may result in filtering out Nodes that should have gone to the Scoring phase (in `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`), or giving low scores to Nodes that should have been given higher scores. (in `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`).

/sig scheduling
/kind feature
/assign

+1 it's good to have API parity

We discussed a bit about this before https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C09TP78DV/p1661093052989079?thread_ts=1661006326.904089&cid=C09TP78DV, and I was thinking why don't we unify the label names in deployment and statefulset(currently they are `pod-template-name` and `controller-revision-hash`), then no need for this matchLabelKeys anymore. I think this is the main case why we need matchLabelKeys for identifying old/new pods.

For third-party controllers, they can also follow the rule.
The key point is kubernetes should provide a mechanism to make scheduler aware of the old/new replicas. Currently, the hash label seems can provide some help.

Found an old issue and seems it has been implemented to use different labels as intended.

> We can use controller-revision-hash for DaemonSet and StatefulSet, and keep Deployment as-is. Deployment hash label key should be different from other two because Deployment pods hash labels is used by selector (unlike the other two controllers).
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/47554

Adding a new well-known label to identify Pod's group might be one general solution instead of unifying the labels of deployment and statefulset. Actually, it's been also discussed when we introduced `MatchLabelKeys`, but we didn't go with it.  (option 1 in the doc.)
https://docs.google.com/document/d/12F1YXsvy4SmumPiL3LHMLnuMHvyMqSzDqF-L9J37ZfA/edit#

Right, because changing the default behavior is not backwards compatible. I think `MatchLabelKeys` gives more flexibility to users. However, it would still be useful to have a well known label, even if they are not the same for each workload API.

> I was thinking why don't we unify the label names in deployment and statefulset(currently they are pod-template-name and controller-revision-hash)

Implicit unifying may sometimes misinterpret user workloads' intentions. For example, if user's intention is to spread app1 AND app2 (both apps with identical labelSelector). During app2's rolling upgrade, with `MatchLabelKeys`, it's user's responsibility to explicitly specify whether to spread app1 + app2's new Pods, or just app2's new Pods, or whatever intention the user wants. So I'm more in favor of an explicit API field.

Adding MatchLabelKeys to other scheduling primitives is a reasonable next step.

Regarding using a common label: we briefly discussed that in the KEP as an alternative. Labels are arbitrary, the scheduler shouldn't really make such strong assumptions about their semantics. What is the concern about MatchLabelKeys?

Thanks for feedbacks, unifying the labels may not be a good choice. 

About `MatchLabelKeys`, I have several concerns:
1) Currently we treat it as a feature option, but I can't image that people will expect scheduling decisions taking read-to-rolling-update pods into consideration. We could say it's not for breaking end-users, but actually the impact is small for that's what they want. 

2) As @ahg-g said, we'd like to apply the `MatchLabelKeys` to other scheduling primitives, it grows the burden of users for they have to configure this for all corresponding plugins(And I think most of the plugins yes). 

3) Besides identifying the old/new replicas in rolling update, does `MatchLabelKeys` have other earnings, from the https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3243., I got no other answers. Please add other cases if you guys have.

In general, MatchLabelKeys can be used to simplify your affinity selectors. Now you only have to specify the label key, instead of having to copy the label value as well.

So that should be some motivation for users to migrate to the new API.

I think the vast majority of pod anti affinity users use it to spread their workloads for availability reasons (across nodes or AZs) so `MatchLabelKeys` is a much easier way to specify that, and much more resilient to changes in naming for example for a workload. A single generic antiAffinity term can be applied for a given labeling convention and that's much more powerful and less repetitive.

Looks worth making a concrete proposal for it, as there are more positive thoughts than negative ones so far.
Opened https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3633, we can continue to discuss it in KEP.

Sorry, I've just confirmed it's wrong.
Here is how the matchLabelKeys are merged with LabelSelector in topology spread.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ead7d66ee12656cfb7c633dd42a87f8d9cfaa469/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/podtopologyspread/common.go#L138-L142

It ignored `!ok` case. So, if the LabelSelector before merging the matchLabelKeys is no-match, but it has matchLabelKeys, the LabelSelector is just ignored and only matchLabelKeys are taken into consideration.

The current logic for MatchLabelKeys in PodAffinity is created while checking the logic in the TopologySpread. So, the current logic for MatchLabelKeys in PodAffinity is the same behavior as the current matchLabelKeys in Topology Spread.

---

So, as a result, the behaviors in each case will be:

1. empty labelSelector = match all:

```
  affinity:
    podAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        - labelSelector: {}
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
```

2. null labelSelector = match nothing:

```
  affinity:
    podAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        - labelSelector: null
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
```

3. empty labelSelector with matchLabelKeys = match with the Pod which has the same label value in "security":

```
  affinity:
    podAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        - labelSelector: {}
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
          matchLabelKeys: 
          - "security"
```


4. null labelSelector with matchLabelKeys = match with the Pod which has the same label value in "security": 
(= the same behavior as (3))

```
  affinity:
    podAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        - labelSelector: null
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
          matchLabelKeys: 
          - "security"
```

Aldo responded already, but re-iterate, a JobSet allows creating [a group of replicated jobs from a template](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/jobset/blob/749a77c2647ac46b309b8227f66293e4116b97ed/api/v1alpha1/jobset_types.go#L90), so the template is shared between all jobs, the user can't change the label per job.

@sanposhiho yes, but the case you have can be done manually (we know the jobset name, so we can explicitly set the value); the case where it is not possible is doing it across jobs within a replicatedJob:

```
spec:
  affinity:
    podAntiAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        - matchLabelSelectors: 
          - matchLabelKey: job-name
            operator NotIn
```

The reason the use can't set the value explicitly is because the template is shared between [all the jobs of a ReplicatedJob](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/jobset/blob/749a77c2647ac46b309b8227f66293e4116b97ed/api/v1alpha1/jobset_types.go#LL95C1-L95C1)

to give a concrete example:

```
affinity:
        podAffinity:  # ensures the pods of this job land on the same rack
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - matchLabelSelectors:
              - matchLabelKey: job-name
              operator: In
             topologyKey: rack
        podAntiAffinity: # ensures only this job lands on the rack
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - matchLabelSelectors:
              - matchLabelKey: job-name
              operator: NotIn
          - labelSelector:
              matchExpressions:
              - key: job-name
                operator: Exists
            namespaceSelector: {}
            topologyKey: rack
```
